gaps.sentence: The audience always ___ when the curtain falls.
gaps.explanation: 'Always' marks a general habit, which takes the present simple: claps.

gaps.sentence: When I came downstairs, the whole house ___ of fresh bread.
gaps.hint: smell as a state verb in past
gaps.explanation: 'Smell' as a state verb takes simple tenses, here the past simple: smelled.

gaps.sentence: No sooner ___ the verdict been read than the defence announced an appeal.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner had … been read than' — past perfect passive with inversion.

gaps.hint: how long plus since needs present perfect
gaps.explanation: 'How long' questions about periods that include the present take the present perfect: have you known.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.

gaps.sentence: I ___ coffee at all, but I drink tea every morning.
gaps.hint: a general habit contrasted with another habit
gaps.explanation: A permanent habit takes the present simple, so the negative form is: don't drink.

gaps.sentence: The play ___ when we reached the theatre, so we missed the first scene.
gaps.hint: it started before we reached it
gaps.explanation: The starting happened before the past moment of arriving, so the past perfect fits: had already started.

gaps.sentence: Our team ___ the championship twice in the last five years.
gaps.hint: in the last five years up to now
gaps.explanation: 'In the last five years' is a period up to the present, so the present perfect fits: has won.
